correctness.rationale: The killed-interval ODE gives exact unreset hitting transforms and free time. First-event conditioning gives the full resetting hitting-time transform and mean. Strict positivity of the explicit second derivative in u=d(L-d) proves convex-order transfer and unique secant/Jensen extremizers. The O(r^2) small-reset difference follows from uniform transform expansion and a variance identity; high-rate ratio follows from endpoint exponential asymptotics, including the antipodal contribution caveat. The standalone finite script passes 921 checks, including an independent finite-difference killed-generator comparison; universal statements rely on proofs, not testing.

originality.rationale: A fixed mean free-search-cost budget forces the new Brownian ring spatial-reset design theorem to compare genuine alternatives. The inspected 2026 ring paper optimizes rates at specified reset sites, the 2024 random-position paper introduces equivalent reset points at prescribed rates, and the 2025 distributed reset paper optimizes rates and density families on a half-line. Their stated results do not imply simultaneous convex-order Laplace optimality for all rates under this constraint. Published-record and literature searches did not identify direct implication. The remaining possibility of broader convex-order renewal theorems is acknowledged; originality is best-knowledge and not independently certified.

value.rationale: The natural free-first-passage-time mean is held equal across reset-site laws, preventing the trivial nearest-reset-site optimization. The complete convex-order hierarchy and sharp unique extreme measures simultaneously hold for every reset rate and positive discounted-hitting-time Laplace parameter; the weak-reset quadratic cancellation and strong-reset exponentially diverging relative advantage show a non-obvious mechanism of distributional heterogeneity. This is a motivated design theorem rather than a routine evaluation of a fixed-site formula.
